clue.text: ABC is specially so

indicators.note: specially here means made over in a special way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that the alphabet's first letters are, in a particular way, elementary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially' rearranges the five letters of ABC IS; the whole clue is also the definition, since ABC means the elementary stuff of a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: The ABC of anything is its rudiments, so to call it fundamental or elementary is exactly right.

clue.text: Indian jet covering short distance

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black
a foot is a short distance

explanation.surface: An aircraft flies over a brief stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jet' suggests an aircraft, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American people of the northern Plains carry this name.

clue.text: Understand, for example, about 23's double

indicators.note: about says one piece goes around the other

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example

indicators.note: double means the letter appears twice, side by side

parts.note: 23 is VERSUS, whose abbreviation is V

explanation.surface: An instruction to grasp something about a lookalike.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 refers to 23-across, whose answer is abbreviated V; doubled it makes VV, inside SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for know or grasp, from the Spanish for to know.

clue.text: Learn lines by heart for talk

parts.note: to con is to learn or study, an old sense
verse is lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Memorising a script for a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by heart' fits CON's sense of committing to memory.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat or hold a conversation means to talk with someone.

clue.text: Piano played with no end of artistry involved this?

definitions.text: Piano played with no end of artistry involved this?

parts.words: Piano played with no end of artistry involved this?
parts.note: a quiet keyboard performance relies on the left-foot device that mutes the strings; also the phrase means to play something down

explanation.surface: A question about what lies behind an endlessly artistic piano performance.
explanation.definitionFit: The left pedal of a piano mutes the tone, so quiet playing is achieved with it; figuratively it means to understate.

clue.text: The famous author Lawrence became

explanation.surface: Something about what a well-known writer named Lawrence turned into.
explanation.walkthrough: T. E. Lawrence (of Arabia) took the name T. E. Shaw when he enlisted in the RAF; George Bernard Shaw was the famous playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw was a celebrated playwright, and Lawrence of Arabia later adopted that surname.

clue.text: Was a mercenary discharged without weapon?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: discharged means set free, freed
a lance is a weapon

explanation.surface: A question whether a hired soldier was released unarmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: FREED goes around LANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval free lances were soldiers for hire; now it means working for several clients.

clue.text: Game originating in Pyrenees, entailing lots of thrilling action

indicators.note: originating in points to where each word starts, its first letter

explanation.surface: A sport from the Pyrenees full of excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is true: this Basque ball game is from the Pyrenees.
explanation.definitionFit: A Basque court sport in which a ball is hurled against a wall with a basket.

clue.text: Follow gospel one's accepted, as holder of certain beliefs

parts.note: to dog is to follow closely

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Matt is the abbreviation for the Gospel of Matthew
one's gives I plus IS

explanation.surface: Follow the gospel and be accepted as a believer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted' puts IS (from "one's", read as one is) inside MATT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who insists dogmatically on rigid principles, holding a fixed creed.

clue.text: Endless agitation as a revolutionary tool

indicators.note: endless means losing its final letter

parts.note: to be in a lather is to be agitated

explanation.surface: Never-ending unrest used by a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests politics; the tool turns things round.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine tool that spins the workpiece while it is cut or shaped.

clue.text: Benefit from important point in court

explanation.surface: Someone gains from a crucial moment in a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests law, but it is the tennis court, where the point after deuce has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit is a gain or edge; in tennis, the point won after deuce carries the same name.

clue.text: Run hard without a break? That's OK

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether running flat out with no rest is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leg it' is British slang for run fast; written 'without a break' (no space) it becomes the slang word for lawful or genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for lawful or above board, so acceptable; the two-word phrase is slang for running away fast.

clue.text: Soundly beats economic expert

indicators.note: soundly here means as spoken rather than thoroughly, flagging a word that sounds alike

parts.note: beats means canes, strikes with a stick

explanation.surface: Someone thoroughly defeats an economist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like an adverb for a decisive win; it signals a homophone. The British economist's name is pronounced like CANES.
explanation.definitionFit: John Maynard Keynes was the most influential British economist of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Defeated a lot of people, in the event

parts.note: defeated means laid low, knocked flat
a race is a large group of people sharing descent

explanation.surface: Many people were beaten during some occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: A flat race is a horse race with no jumps, a British racing term.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse race over level ground without fences is a fixture on a race card, an event.

clue.text: Reportedly purchase weapon with support of both sides

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so a word that sounds like purchase

parts.note: to purchase is to buy
a partisan is a long-handled spear, a type of halberd

explanation.surface: Someone said to be buying arms with backing from both camps.
explanation.walkthrough: A partisan is also a pole weapon with a broad blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Supported by two political parties, which is the backing of both sides.

clue.text: Knowing all income isn't redistributed

indicators.note: redistributed means shared out afresh, so the letters are dealt into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that earnings are not being reallocated, by someone fully informed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redistributed' rearranges the letters of INCOME ISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Having infinite awareness, as a god is said to have, means being aware of everything.

clue.text: Discovering top's off, narrowly averted disaster

indicators.note: top's off says the first letter, the top of a down entry, is removed

parts.note: unearthing means discovering, digging up

explanation.surface: Finding the lid has come off, a calamity barely avoided.
explanation.definitionFit: A close call or narrow escape, where disaster almost happened.

clue.text: Proceed with difficulty, lacking vitality

explanation.surface: Someone struggles onward, tired and listless.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobble along is to walk with a halting gait; as an adjective it means floppy, without energy.

clue.text: Left aboard, sailor consumes top-class cheese

parts.note: on a ship the left side is the port side

indicators.note: consumes means eats, taking in another piece

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor
U means upper-class, top-class

explanation.surface: A sailor on a ship eats fine cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: U is British slang for upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild French cow's-milk cheese made originally by Trappist monks.

clue.text: Splendid fun I had, protected from rain

indicators.note: protected means kept inside a covering, so one piece is put within another

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat, a shield from rain
a jest is a bit of fun

explanation.surface: Someone enjoyed themselves while sheltered from a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protected' puts JEST and I inside MAC, the British short word for a mackintosh raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand and dignified in appearance, regal and stately.

clue.text: Drivers try to avoid this carriage

explanation.surface: Motorists steer clear of a particular vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a speed trap; a trap is also a light two-wheeled horse-drawn cart.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorists dodge a police speed check; a pony and trap is a small horse-drawn vehicle.

clue.text: Criminal element he leads

parts.note: he refers to a man, a male
a factor is an element or component of something

explanation.surface: A man heads a criminal component.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer or felon; the Latin-derived word means one who does evil.

clue.text: As centre half in match. I seldom cheat

indicators.note: in says the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A footballer playing central defence says they rarely cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As centre half' is football scene-setting (a central defender); the letters run across 'match I seldom'.
explanation.definitionFit: To swindle or defraud someone, informal sense of a woodworking verb.

clue.text: Latest photographs showing experts

parts.note: the hottest news is the latest, so hot means latest
shots are photographs

explanation.surface: The newest pictures display skilled people.
explanation.definitionFit: Highly skilled or successful people are called aces or high-flyers in this slang.

clue.text: Butterfly common in Hampstead, for example

explanation.surface: A butterfly often seen in a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampstead Heath is a large public common in north London; the heath is also a small brown butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: Several butterflies such as the small heath have this name; open common land is called this too.

clue.text: In any case, it divides the sides

definitions.text: In any case, it divides the sides

parts.words: In any case, it divides the sides
parts.note: a lawsuit is named as one party against another, with a small Latin word set between the two names

explanation.surface: A general remark that something always separates two teams.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for against stands between the plaintiff and defendant in a case title.

clue.text: Suspicious and wary about poster

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: shy means cautious, wary
an ad is a poster or advertisement

explanation.surface: Someone distrustful and cautious about a placard.
explanation.definitionFit: Disreputable or dubious, giving cause for doubt.

clue.text: Executes females? Not by the sound of it

explanation.surface: A shocked question about putting women to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not by the sound of it': the two senses are spelt the same but said differently, one rhyming with buzz, the other with doze.
explanation.definitionFit: Executes means carries out, a verb; female deer and rabbits are called by this plural.

clue.text: No wife can be so wrong

explanation.surface: A comment that no wife could be so mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as A MISS: an unmarried woman is no wife.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried woman is titled a Miss, so not a wife; as one word it means faulty or awry.

clue.text: Deficiency associated with long American winter?

explanation.surface: A shortage linked to a lengthy US winter.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans call autumn the fall; a brief autumn goes with a long winter.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortfall is a deficit; read as two words it is a brief American autumn.

clue.text: It's hard dashing madly round lake in mountain region

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: round says the word dashing goes around the lake letter before the shuffle
madly says the letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters that are shuffled
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Someone races wildly round a loch in hill country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' rearranges DASHING with L (lake) placed among them, 'round' telling us the lake goes inside; H for hard comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountainous north of Scotland is known by this name; generally it means upland country.

clue.text: Keen, exercising for vault

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry in grief
PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: An enthusiast working out in preparation for a leap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager; it is the verb meaning to wail. 'vault' looks like a gymnastic leap, but it is an underground chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground chamber beneath a church, often used for burials.
